references.text: The people respond in a similar way that they will do everything the Lord has said, which shows their commitment to the covenant.
The people give the same answer earlier in the chapter, confirming their obedience to the Lord's word.
Moses refers to the people's promise to hear and do all that the Lord commands.
The law is to be read aloud to the people, just as the book of the covenant was read aloud to the people of Israel.
The people renew their commitment to serve the Lord and listen to his voice.
The king reads the book of the covenant to the people, and they commit themselves to keep the covenant.
Ezra reads the book of the law to the people who had gathered, in a similar way as Moses read the book of the covenant.
The letter to the Hebrews refers to this event where Moses proclaimed all the commandments to the people and confirmed the covenant.
A historical parallel where a rediscovered book of the covenant is read aloud to restore the covenant relationship.
A parallel account of the same event as in 2 Kings, emphasizing the role of reading before the making of the covenant.
The completion of the covenant cycle: from reading (Exodus) to the commitment of the heart (Josiah).
A parallel to 2 Kings 23:3 showing the renewal of the covenant based on the words of Scripture.
A thematic parallel to the people's immediate 'yes' to obey God's word in a situation of correction.
God's direct response to and confirmation of the people's promise of obedience.
